newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economy recovering slowly -- BOJ quoted.
newsitem.headline: Japan economy recovering slowly -- BOJ quoted.

text.p: Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Wednesday that the central bank's branch managers had all agreed that Japan's economy was recovering slowly, according to an official of the Japan Federation of Economic Organisations (Keidanran).
Matsushita's remarks were made during a meeting of BOJ and Keidanran executives, the official said.
Matsushita was quoted as summarising a two-day meeting of BOJ branch managers that ended on Tuesday by saying:

"The economy marked time slightly in the summer, but looking at the progress in the autumn, the branch managers agreed that there was no change in the BOJ's view that the economy is gradually recovering."
Matsushita was quoted as saying that the mechanism for a self-sustainable recovery was in place and had started working.
"Japan's economy may continue to recover even if there is a change in public works spending," he was quoted as saying.
He said capital spending was recovering on the back of improved corporate earnings, while private consumption was also improving.
Economists say public works spending is expected to shrink in the autumn, or later, following massive injections of public funds to stimulate the economy in the past year.
Matsushita was also quoted as saying the economy had not picked up as expected, despite the fact the official discount rate had been kept at a record-low 0.5 percent for more than a year.
"We feel that the pressure on the economy from structural adjustment has been excessive," he said.
